intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that Pallister-Hall-like syndrome (PHLS) is caused by biallelic germline mutation in the SMO gene (601500) on chromosome 7q32.

paragraphs.text: Pallister-Hall-like syndrome is a developmental disorder in which hypothalamic hamartoma occurs with polydactyly. Other reported features include microcephaly, atrioventricular septal defect, narrow chest, shortening of the long bones, and intestinal aganglionosis (Rubino et al., 2019; Le et al., 2020).

paragraphs.text: Encha-Razavi et al. (1992) proposed that hypothalamic hamartoma with skeletal dysplasia and oro-facial abnormalities be treated as the minimum criteria for a distinct, possibly familial entity, which they called 'congenital hypothalamic hamartoma syndrome' (CHHS). In their analysis of reported cases of Pallister-Hall syndrome, skeletal dysplasia and oro-facial abnormalities were the only features that were always present. As far as they knew, isolated skeletal dysplasia with congenital hypothalamic hamartoma had not been reported before.

paragraphs.text: Encha-Razavi et al. (1992) found congenital hypothalamic hamartomas at autopsy in 3 unrelated fetuses. In the first 2 fetuses, the tumor occurred with skeletal dysplasia only. In the third fetus, the tumor was part of a nonrandom association of congenital malformations suggestive of Meckel syndrome. In one of the families, a previous boy had died soon after birth with similar craniofacial and skeletal abnormalities.

paragraphs.text: Craig et al. (2008) compared paired blood and resected tumor DNA from 55 patients with sporadic, nonsyndromic hypothalamic hamartoma and intractable epilepsy. Resequencing of GLI3 found no causative germline mutations. However, 8 of the 55 (15%) hamartoma tissue samples had somatic chromosomal abnormalities that included the GLI3 locus. One sample had a 7p copy-number abnormality. Eight samples had loss of heterozygosity within GLI3: 3 were found by resequencing and 5 more by genotyping 28 SNPs. Craig et al. (2008) concluded that chromosomal abnormalities within GLI3 are associated with the pathogenesis of hypothalamic hamartoma in sporadic, nonsyndromic patients, and noted that these somatic mutations appeared to be highly variable.

paragraphs.text: In cells from individuals with biallelic SMO variants, Le et al. (2020) found that ciliogenesis was normal but hedgehog signal transduction was severely altered. This resulted either from altered trafficking in the primary cilium or from abnormal activation of the pathway downstream of SMO. GLI2 accumulated at the cilium tip independently of hedgehog, suggesting that SMO may regulate basal ciliary trafficking of GLI2 when the pathway is off.
